name: The Bellworks
entry:
The Bellworks occupy Fogport's northeastern heights: a forest of smoke-blackened fog-harvest factories, yards, and loading spurs looking down over the city. From above, their rooftops resemble a field of enormous metal flowers.

The Bellworks do not make Fogport's emerald mist. They harvest it. Each great Fog Condenser Work rises five or six stories and is crowned with giant brass-and-iron intake bells shaped like antique phonograph speakers. Their flared mouths turn upward into the weather, striped in chipped warning paint and marked with enormous faded numbers. When a green bank rolls in, the bells open wide and draw it down through pipes, cooling coils, and clattering condenser towers.

The result is bottled fog concentrate—especially the valuable, thick-grade Heavy Fog—used in alchemy, refrigeration, pneumatic machinery, precision instruments, medicine, and carefully limited concealment work. Sealed canisters leave by tram and ship for every corner of the industrialized world. On strong harvest days the works run around the clock: whistles cut through the haze, tiny crews cross high catwalks with lanterns and tool bags, and copper fog wagons drink mist straight from the streets.

Fogporters call the industry the condensers, but the district is the Bellworks. Its people are practical, union-minded, and deeply suspicious of anyone who calls fog “mere weather.” The air smells of wet iron, hot oil, salt, and something faintly medicinal.
